data.title: Salicylic acid (6% ointment, paint)
data.summary: VI Keratolytics & emollients · β-hydroxy acid; keratolytic (desmolytic) agent
data.body:
_Topicals · VI Keratolytics & emollients_

**Class:** β-hydroxy acid; keratolytic (desmolytic) agent

## Mechanism of action
- Dissolves the intercellular cement (desmosomes) between corneocytes, so scale sheds — 'desmolytic' rather than true keratolytic
- Lipophilic — penetrates the pilosebaceous unit (comedolytic)
- Mild antibacterial/antifungal; enhances penetration of other topicals

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- 3–6%: psoriasis plaques and scalp, ichthyosis, palmoplantar keratoderma, seborrhoeic dermatitis (shampoo), hyperkeratotic eczema
- 0.5–2%: acne washes and gels (comedolytic)
- Salicylic acid paint/collodion (10–20% with lactic acid): common and plantar warts, corns, calluses
- 40% plaster: corns, plantar warts
- 20–30% peels: acne, PIH (see chemical peels)

## Dose & formulations
- 6% ointment/cream: once or twice daily to thick scaly areas
- Wart paint: soak wart, pare, apply daily to the wart only (protect surrounding skin with petroleum jelly), for up to 12 weeks

## Adverse effects
- Irritation, peeling, stinging
- Salicylism (salicylate toxicity) with use over large areas, high concentrations, broken skin, children, renal impairment: nausea, tinnitus, hyperventilation, confusion, metabolic acidosis
- Ulceration of normal skin around warts

## Contraindications
- Children under 2 years; large areas (over about 20% BSA) in children
- Diabetics and peripheral vascular disease (wart paints on feet — ulceration risk)
- Aspirin allergy (relative); renal impairment

## Drug interactions
- Methotrexate, sulfonylureas, warfarin — absorbed salicylate can increase their effects

## Pregnancy & lactation
Small areas acceptable; avoid large-area or high-concentration use.

## Viva points
- Desmolytic — dissolves the cement between cells
- Salicylism in children treated over large areas
- Avoid wart paints on diabetic feet

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.55 (Agents used for hyperkeratosis); Khopkar ch.27 (Moisturizers and keratolytic agents). Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
